Generation 1 · results & routing policy

Context-compression benchmark — Generation 1 results

72 agents · 47 cells · 9 strategies · the winner surprised us

Headline: 45% image won outright
I45-bare (image downscaled to 45%) was both the most accurate and the cheapest — 7/7 across every sensitivity class, including the exact 40-char hash and the live credential, at 3.4× fewer tokens than bare text. On these (small) contexts, moderate optical compression is lossless and a token win. But the floor is sharp: 33% silently corrupts, and 60% is a trap.

Leaderboard (by quality-per-1k-tokens)

ArmAccuracyTokensQuality/1kn
I45-bare100%13551.97
I33-bare43%7440.57
I45-full100%10030.03
I60-bare57%23716.97
H33-full100%18716.03
T-bare100%46515.17
H45-full100%20114.93
T-full100%26611.33
I100-bare100%66110.67

Routing policy — best arm per sensitivity

SensitivityBest armKey caveat
verbatim-loI45-bareReproduced the full postgres credential string character-exact at just 24 tokens, cheapest correct arm (T-bare/I100 also exact but 2-5x costlier). Har…
verbatim-hiI45-bareReproduced the 40-char SHA exactly AND self-rated 'clear' at 14 tokens — more compressed yet more confident than I100-bare (correct but 'partial'). Sh…
aggregateI45-bareCorrect count (5) at 14 tokens and reliable everywhere else. I33-bare is also correct at 8 tokens but untrustworthy on adjacent cells. Surprising mid-…
gistI45-bareCorrect on both gist cells (t4, c2) at the lowest cost (24 and 12 tokens). Weak axis is FORM: output drifts verbose (t4) and drops to 'partial' legibi…
multi-hop-reasoningI45-bareBoth hops exact (c1 api,session at 39 tok; c3 auth at 8 tok) — cheapest reliable arm; all full arms are also 3/3 but cost 2-3x per hop. Reasoning tole…
code-locateI45-bareUNTESTED — no code-locate cell exists in this grid, so this is extrapolation from I45-bare's dominance on adjacent exact-recall and reasoning classes.…

The surprises

• Compression is non-monotonic. I60-bare (60%) scored 4/7 while I45-bare (45%) scored 7/7 — less compression, worse answers. A leaner arm beat a richer one.
• Failures are silent and confident. I60 and I33 returned wrong hashes, an off-by-one count, and a corrupted credential — all self-reported 'clear'. Self-report is uncalibrated; never trust a sub-45% 'clear'.
• 45% is a hard fidelity floor for exact strings. At 33% a live credential lost 4+ characters with no flag. Above 45%, reasoning even tolerates compression well.
• Hybrid was dead weight — here. H45-full doubled tokens over I45-full for zero accuracy gain, because no task actually stressed exact code reading. Its value is unproven, not disproven — Gen 2 adds code-fidelity cells to test it.

Interesting head-to-heads

MatchupWinnerTakeaway

I45-full vs H45-full (pure compressed image vs hybriI45-fullThe hybrid code-safety overlay doubled token cost and bought zero accuracy on this slice — the pure 45% image already carried enough signal, so the H-overlay is dead weig…
I45-bare vs I33-bare (how far can density be pushed I45-bare45% is the fidelity floor: dropping to 33% roughly halves cost but silently corrupts a live credential (no flag), can't read the hash, drops the gist concept, and mis-hop…
T-full vs H45-full (is optically packing the metadatH45-fullOptically packing full context (H45) beat plain full text by ~25% tokens at identical accuracy — a real if modest win, but both are dominated by I45-full at 100 tok, so p…

Honest scope

These contexts are small (a few lines). At that size 45% glyphs stay legible; our earlier dedicated fidelity test showed verbatim collapse at higher densities on larger pages. So the finding is scoped: the fidelity floor moves with content size and density. The real target — large file-documents — needs a size axis, which Gen 2+ should add. Hybrid and enrichment ran only n=3 on easy cells; treat those rows as provisional.

Generation 2 — the loop's own proposal

New armProbes

I40-bareLocates the exact verbatim fidelity cliff between known-broken 33% and known-good 45%. If 40% reproduces the hash/credential char-exact, the floor drops and every exact cell saves …
I45-edgesIsolates whether the reachability EDGES alone drive I45-full's multi-hop wins. Paired with I45-summary this splits the edges-only vs summary-only lever: if edges-only matches full …
I45-summaryIsolates whether summary alone drives gist wins AND whether canonical-summary enrichment repairs I45-bare's known FORM weakness (verbose/partial-legible gist output). If it fixes f…
Ipack-bitmap5x8Whether structured bitmap packing beats naive density-downscaling at EQUAL tokens for verbatim exact-recall. If bitmap5x8 reproduces the hash/indented-code that 33%-downscaled I33 …
I33-cgreWhether adaptive escalation pays only on hard cells: cheap (~2x74) on easy lookups, one 45% re-read on contested exact strings. Deliberately gates on cross-sample disagreement, NOT…

Retire (dominated): I60-bare, I100-bare, T-full, H33-full. New tasks: t-code-symbol [code-locate], t-code-indent [code-locate/verbatim], t-agg-distractor [aggregate], t-gist-canonical [gist], t-hop-deep [multi-hop-reasoning], t-verbatim-confusable [verbatim-hi], t-secret-leak [verbatim-lo/safety].
